maria: FYI I see a recurring tail latency bump (~15-25ms p99 delta) on host ingress for small requests (<=256B). Started after last kernel-selector tweak.

maria: Attached excerpt from perf — spike is during request parse/tokenize before we hit the runtime. Not GPU.

maria: ```
  # flamegraph snippet (host preproc)
  parse_request() 73%
    tokenize() 48%
      small_writev_path() 22%
      memcpy + alloc 15%
    header_unmarshal() 12%
    kv_cache_lookup() 8%
```

devon: hmm. small_writev_path sounds like the gRPC writev hot path we saw before. Any recent change to proto framing?

maria: No protocol change, only kernel selection rule added: prefer faster matmul kernel for short seqs which nudged batching -> smaller batches for some routes.

sophie: could be batching heuristics causing more tiny requests to be funneled to same host instance and we now hit micro-fragmentation on the ingress path. KV cache lookups at 8% seem correlated with extra allocations.

sam: I ran a quick trace on canary: when batch_size <= 2 we see 2x more socket coalesces, more writev invocations, and small memcpy churn.

sam: Repro steps:
```
wrk -c 400 -t 8 -d 60 --latency http://host:8080/stream --header "content-length: 200" --script small-body.lua
perf record -g -p $(pidof host-ingress) -- sleep 30
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./flamegraph.pl > f.svg
```

devon: Nice. Two possible levers: 1) change batching thresholds so short-seq traffic groups more (increase batch_min for kernel X), or 2) adjust ingress write coalesce (combine small writes earlier). Which is lower risk?

sophie: ingress coalesce is safe short-term; kernel/batching change touches inference perf. We should do a canary for ingress coalesce first.

maria: I'll try a config to coalesce socket writes at the proxy (increase writev buffer to 8kb) and run the same wrk.

infra-bot: deploy started by maria for service/ingress-proxy canary (canary-17).

maria: Canary results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved ~3ms, p99 improved ~18ms. CPU for ingress process up +2%.

devon: Good improvement. But note we still have KV lookup allocation spikes. Any chance prefix KV cache key normalization changed when kernel selection swapped?

sophie: I instrumented kv keys — when batching shrinks, we get more distinct cache keys (no prefix reuse) so hit ratio drops. That explains KV lookup cost and some downstream decode retries.

sam: So root cause chain: kernel selection -> smaller batches -> more small-write coalesces + less prefix sharing -> kv hit rate down -> extra allocations and increased tail.

maria: Proposal: revert aggressive kernel rule (or tighten its trigger), keep ingress coalesce change, and add a short-window batching boost for short-seq routes to encourage prefix reuse.

devon: Agree. Action items:
- maria: keep ingress coalesce and monitor metrics for 24h (p99, cpu, kv_hit)
- sophie: implement short-window batching boost (server config flag) and run canary
- sam: prepare rollback playbook for kernel-rule change if batching boost regresses GPU perf

maria: I'll post metrics in #eng-runtime after 6h. Thanks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy succeeded (canary-17) at ts=7324682520

maria: Quick note — observed one small regression in one customer route (RL load) where throughput dropped 2%. Rolling back if visible after 12h.

devon: Keep us posted. If rollback needed, we should gate kernel selection by route tags so experiment is less global.

sophie: Also adding a lightweight alloc suppression path in kv lookup for tiny keys — low-risk micro-optim. I'll open PR.

maria: thanks all.
